summary: Port is byte-identical to the original on every frame I dumped, across five rigs, four frame rates, three seeds, two wall clocks and a late (t=240 s) window — three red dots marching right at exactly 10 px/s over a full-blue strip.
observations: Both sides draw the same picture: the whole strip full blue (0,0,255) with exactly three pure-red (255,0,0) pixels evenly spaced at pixelCount/3 apart. On the 60 px default rig that is indices {k, k+20, k+40}; meanR 13 (=3/60x255) and meanB 242 (=57/60x255) on BOTH sides in every run.

Motion: the trio steps RIGHT by exactly 1 pixel every 0.1 s and wraps at the N/3 spacing. On the default rig the lit index is (1+floor(10*t)) mod 20 on both sides — verified at t=0/0.05/0.1/0.15/0.5/1.0/2.35/3.7/5.95 (orig 1,1,2,2,6,11,4,18,0; port identical). Wrap period 2.0 s on 60 px.

The 10 px/s tick is ABSOLUTE, not a strip fraction: at --pixels 300 the offset is (1+floor(10t)) mod 100 (10 px/s, 10 s wrap) and at --pixels 12 it is (1+floor(10t)) mod 4 (10 px/s, 0.4 s wrap). Both sides follow the identical law at all three sizes.

Time-based, not frame-coupled, on both sides: rendering at --fps 10/20/40/100 puts the dots at the SAME indices at the same absolute times (t=0 -> [1,21,41]; t=1 -> [11,31,51]; t=2 -> [1,21,41]; t=3.9 -> [0,20,40]) with orig==port at every sample. The tick-quantisation is finer than the 20 fps grid (0.1 s tick vs 0.05 s frame), so the dumps resolve it honestly rather than aliasing it.

Degenerate-rig agreement: at --pixels 7 the N/3 spacing rounds so that FOUR pixels light on some frames ([0,2,4,6]) and three on others ([1,3,5]). The port reproduces that rounding artefact exactly, frame for frame — same on --grid 16x16 and --grid 32x8, where t=0 lights flat indices [0,85,170,255] (four dots, 256/3 spacing) on both sides.

Index-only on both sides: the flat pixel sequences from --grid 16x16 and --grid 32x8 are byte-identical to each other (and to each other's port), i.e. neither side consults (x,y) — the port matches the original's index-driven character.

Survey (60 s @ 5 fps) shows a single uniform regime — evenly spaced red diagonals, no mode rotation, no palette walk, no drift. All six per-frame series in stats.json (meanBrightness/meanR/meanG/meanB/motion/motionLit) are element-for-element equal between orig and port over all 300 survey frames.

Steady state confirmed: a --skip 240 --seconds 20 --fps 20 window (t=240-260 s) is still orig==port byte-identical, still mean 85, motion series still the clean 17,0,17,0,... alternation (17 on the 0.1 s tick frames, 0 on the in-between frames). No decay, no freeze, no accumulation.

Non-determinism ruled out: --seed 7, --seed 1234 and --wall-clock 1700123456 all produce the identical render on both sides (t=0 [1,21,41], t=1.1 [12,32,52], t=3.9 [0,20,40]), so the pattern is seed- and clock-independent and no RNG-character judgement is needed.
Control surfaces match: --probe-controls reports '(no settable controls)' for BOTH sides. No missing, extra, renamed or re-kinded dial.
feedback: Nothing to fix. Every measurement I could make from rendered output (pixel values, dot count, spacing law, step rate, wrap period, fps-invariance, index-vs-coordinate character, rounding behaviour on degenerate rigs, late-window steady state) is byte-identical between original and port.

If a future change touches this port, the cheap regression check is a --dump at t=0/0.5/1/2.35/3.7 on the default 60 px strip: lit indices must be (1+floor(10t)) mod 20 plus +20/+40, colour exactly (255,0,0) on red and (0,0,255) everywhere else.
